messages:
From: Daniel Cho <billing@clearwave.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: finance@clearwave.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected spike on Dec invoice — requesting reconciliation

Jonas,

We're seeing a ~$4.2k overage on our December invoice compared to the run rate we expected for streaming-embeddings. I've attached our export (clearwave_usage_export_202612.csv) showing several large sessions on 2026-12-21 and 2026-12-27 that don't match our internal activity.

To be specific: the per-request attribution in the invoice shows repeated high token counts for session IDs that our logs indicate were short (single-digit turns). Can you help reconcile how those sessions were charged? We need an explanation and a proposed remediation before we finalize payment.

Attached: clearwave_usage_export_202612.csv (CSV, 48KB)

Thanks,
Daniel Cho
Finance Ops
ClearWave Analytics

For traceability, I'm creating a ticket in our billing queue and will share the reference once it's open.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on Dec invoice — requesting reconciliation

Hi all — I dug into the raw metering and the debug traces referenced by Jonas. Summary of findings (short version):

1) Root cause: duplicate attribution from streaming chunk retries + session id reuse
- ClearWave used our streaming-embeddings endpoint with multi-chunk uploads on the dates you highlighted.
- We observed a client-side retry pattern: when the client dropped a connection mid-upload, their client retried the same session id and re-sent chunks. Because our metering logic at the time was counting tokens on receipt of each chunk and did not dedupe by (session id, chunk-range) for streaming uploads, some chunks were counted twice.

2) Scope and impact:
- Affected window: 2026-12-20 00:00 UTC -> 2026-12-28 23:59 UTC
- A subset of sessions from ClearWave show double-counting; other customers had similar transient cases but at much lower volumes.
- Estimated overcount for ClearWave: ~2.1M tokens (our conservative estimate), which maps to roughly $3.9k in billable amount at your rate tier.

3) Fixes applied / rollout:
- We deployed a hotfix to the streaming metering layer on 2027-01-14 11:10 UTC that deduplicates (session_id, chunk_index) and adds a short-lived idempotency window for replayed chunks. The hotfix is live in all regions.
- We've also pushed an SDK note recommending exponential backoff and unique session ids per upload (patch queued: SDK v2.7.1).

4) Proposed remediation:
- Immediate credit for the estimated overcount: $3,900.
- We will re-run the December window against the deduped metering and share a reconciliation CSV by EOD 2027-01-15. If the reconciliation shows a materially different number (>10% delta), we'll adjust the credit accordingly.
- Preventative: in addition to the hotfix, we'll add a post-aggregation check to detect similar spikes and alert both Redwood ops and affected customers.

Attachments: redwood-debug-trace-9876.txt (server-side trace excerpt showing duplicate chunk receipts)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Daniel — thanks for your patience while we completed the reconciliation. Per Rishi's analysis we confirmed a net overcount of 2,089,740 tokens across the window you flagged. We've issued a credit of $3,900 against invoice INV-202612-034 and created credit memo CM-20270115-112.

What we did:
- Applied credit CM-20270115-112 to your account; you'll see the adjustment on the January statement.
- Deployed metering dedupe hotfix (2027-01-14 11:10 UTC) and SDK guidance; engineering will monitor for recurrence.
- Attached: reconciliation CSV and the trace excerpt we used for verification (available in the shared drive link).

If you'd prefer a standalone refund instead of credit on the January statement, we can open a payments request — just say the word and Lauren will start processing.

Thanks again for raising this — sorry for the disruption, and please reach out directly if anything else looks off.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Billing Manager
Redwood Inference
